# Run CAST locally

Most people use CAST through its hosted website and never need to install
anything. Run it locally only if you want your **own** private instance — for
teaching, offline use, or development.

CAST ships as a Docker Compose stack (web app, interactive model pages, database
and numerical solver together), so a full instance starts with one command. You
do **not** need to install Python, MySQL or MODFLOW yourself — they live inside
the containers.

## Prerequisites

- [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/) with Docker Compose v2
- Git

## 1. Get the code

```bash
git clone --branch Personal-CAST-development https://github.com/CAST-IIT/CAST.git cast
cd cast
```

## 2. Configure

Copy the template and fill in a few values:

```bash
cp .env.example .env
```

In `.env` set:

| Variable | Value |
|---|---|
| `SECRET_KEY` | Generate one: `python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(48))"` |
| `DB_USER`, `DB_PASSWORD`, `MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD` | Any passwords you choose for the local database |
| `SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE` | `false` for local `http://localhost` (otherwise you can't stay logged in) |

The other defaults already point at localhost and can be left as they are.

## 3. Start

```bash
docker compose up --build -d
```

When the containers are up, open **<http://localhost:5000>** and
[register an account](accounts.qmd) to begin.

## Stop and update

```bash
docker compose down          # stop
git pull && docker compose up --build -d   # update to the latest version
```

Your accounts and site data live in the database volume and survive updates.
